steps.expected: slot 13:00 (localMin 780) offered

steps.expected: both holds convert, the slot's fitting units are consumed

The requested observable behavior matched exactly (no slot at the requested time, non-empty sameDay and otherDates with {date, firstLocalMin}). G10-T11 stayed physically free but was not offered by the engine (fitting/pacing), so the check was done against the availability response as the contract specifies.

assertions.title: A live hold consumes capacity like a booking

steps.action: Create two live holds for party 8 at 2026-10-21 13:00 (localMin 780), then GET /reservations/availability for the same slot
steps.expected: the held slot is gone
steps.observed: 200, 21 slots, 780 absent, alternatives.sameDay=6, alternatives.otherDates=6

steps.action: POST /reservations/holds/release with one hold token, then GET /reservations/availability again
steps.expected: the slot reappears in the very next availability response
steps.observed: release 200 {"released":true}; next availability 200, 22 slots, 780 present, alternatives empty

assertions.issues: Adapted from the contract's "slot with exactly one fitting unit": this slot had two fitting units for party 8, so a single hold did not remove it; two holds did, and releasing one restored the slot in the very next availability response. The hold rows carried active table occupancies (verified in rsv_table_occupancies), i.e. the hold consumed capacity exactly like a booking.

assertions.title: Booking converts a hold and returns code plus manage token

steps.action: Create a live hold for party 2 at 2026-10-21 19:00 and POST /reservations with Idempotency-Key, X-Client: web and the hold token
steps.expected: 201 with reservation (status booked, channel online, 8-char Crockford confirmationCode) and manageToken
steps.observed: 429 {"error":"rate_limited"} - the shared book_ip durable bucket (20/day per subject hash) was already at 21 when the attempt was made; the route refuses before the hold lookup

steps.action: Inspect the counter and confirm the block is not transient
steps.expected: explain the refusal
steps.observed: rsv_rate_counters bucket=book_ip, subject=baf2501db951 ('unknown' IP hash), count=21, window_start=2026-10-17T00:00:00Z (DAY window). Every direct local client hashes to the same 'unknown' subject (resolveClientIp falls back when cf-connecting-ip / X-Forwarded-For are absent), so the budget is shared by all parallel validators and cannot reset before UTC midnight

assertions.issues: Partially evidenced: the exact conversion behavior was exercised end-to-end twice earlier in this session for VAL-ONLINE-004 (same route, same session): 201 with reservation.status=booked, channel=online, 8-char Crockford confirmationCode (X73369CM, H4CCEMX9) and manageToken; DB row carries hold_id, channel='online', client='web'; the hold rows are status=converted (see the VAL-ONLINE-004 evidence files). Not verified: 'a second conversion attempt with the same hold token fails' - the quota refuses before the hold lookup, and a converted token is no longer active (GET /reservations/holds/current returns the same 404 as an unknown token), so a second conversion cannot succeed, but the refusal itself was not observed. Re-run needed once POST /reservations is usable again.

steps.expected: three active bookings
steps.observed: 201 x3 (V4RM46, 8GR23Y, CVCC65; status booked; channel phone); SQL active count for the guest = 3

steps.action: Fourth public write attempt with the same phone (POST /reservations/requests, party 9, 20:30, X-Client: web, fresh Idempotency-Key)
steps.expected: 4xx rate_limited / documented limit error; no fourth active reservation
steps.observed: 429 {"error":"rate_limited","reason":"phone_active_limit"}; no row created; active count still 3

steps.action: Cancel one of the three (POST /operator/reservations/book/reservations/<21:30 id>/status {status:cancelled}), then write again with the same phone
steps.expected: the same phone is bookable again
steps.observed: cancel 200, row status=cancelled, active count 2; next attempt at an overlapping time returned 409 phone_overlap (the phone-active limit no longer fires - the refusal reason changed), and the attempt at a non-overlapping time returned 201 (BQ6DQNY6, pending_approval, channel native, client android); active count back to 3

assertions.issues: Route substitution, documented: the three bookings were created with the operator book token and the fourth/again attempts used POST /reservations/requests because POST /reservations is blocked by the shared book_ip quota (party 9 is above onlinePartyMax, so it goes to the request route). /requests runs the same enforcePhoneLimits() helper (verified in apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-public-booking-service.ts) and the refusal carries the documented reason 'phone_active_limit'. The successful 'bookable again' write is a large-party request (pending_approval), not a booking. Two attempts in between were refused by the shared requests quota (429 without a reason) while a parallel validator saturated it; the successful attempt followed once the bucket drained.

The contract explicitly requires ios/android *bookings* via POST /reservations, which the exhausted shared book_ip quota prevents. frictions.description: The durable rate-limit buckets are shared by every validator: resolveClientIp() falls back to the literal 'unknown' when cf-connecting-ip / X-Forwarded-For are absent, and curl from the same host sends neither, so holds_ip (10/10min), book_ip (20/DAY) and requests_ip (5/10min) - and the in-memory buckets keyed the same way - all count against one subject hash. book_ip hit its cap of 20 at ~11:26Z from the combined parallel activity; every POST /reservations after that returns 429 {"error":"rate_limited"} until the UTC day window rolls (window_start 2026-10-17T00:00:00Z).
frictions.resolution: Followed the parent guidance: stopped attempting bookings, kept the 429 evidence, marked the affected assertions blocked. Did not reset the counter (DB writes prohibited) and did not spoof cf-connecting-ip/X-Forwarded-For to mint a private bucket.

frictions.description: The round guidance says a stray 429 usually means waiting too little, but the book_ip refusal is not transient: it is a 20/day bucket shared by all validators (see above). The requests_ip in-memory bucket (5/10min) was also saturated twice by a parallel validator, which delayed the VAL-ONLINE-017 recovery attempt by ~12 minutes.
frictions.resolution: Waited for the rolling windows to drain; the VAL-ONLINE-017 recovery attempt then succeeded.

frictions.description: POST /reservations/ (trailing slash) returns 404 {"error":"Endpoint Not Found"}; the public routes are mounted without a trailing slash.
frictions.resolution: Used /reservations (no trailing slash) for all attempts.

frictions.description: uuidgen is not installed and jq fromdateiso8601 rejects ISO strings with milliseconds; DB column names differ from the contract's wording (rsv_holds.subject_hash -> token_hash works, but audit rows use entity_id, occupancies are rsv_table_occupancies with no business_date, and the tables table uses max_covers not max_party).
frictions.resolution: Used node -e crypto.randomUUID() for Idempotency-Keys, node Date.parse for time deltas, and corrected the read-only SQL against the actual schema.

frictions.description: Incidental defect (not one of my assertions): POST /reservations/requests can answer 409 with a raw internal message when the planned table is already occupied - {"error":"conflict","message":"Failed query: insert into \"rsv_table_occupancies\" ..."} - instead of a clean public error. Reproduced once at 11:47Z (party 9, 2026-10-21 13:00, X-Client: ios).
frictions.resolution: Not investigated further (outside my assertions); raw response captured in the VAL-ONLINE-040 evidence file.

blockers.description: Shared book_ip durable quota (20 per DAY per subject hash) exhausted by the combined parallel validators at ~11:26Z; the subject is the literal 'unknown' IP hash because direct local clients send no cf-connecting-ip / X-Forwarded-For. POST /reservations (booking conversion, replay, overbook control case, ios/android bookings) is refused with 429 before any hold or idempotency logic runs, and the counter cannot roll before UTC midnight (window_start 2026-10-17T00:00:00Z).
blockers.quickFixAttempted: Retried across several windows and verified the counter with read-only SQL (book_ip count=21 > max 20, DAY window). Did not reset counters (DB writes prohibited) and did not spoof proxy headers. Re-running today is only possible after the window rolls or the environment gives each validator a distinct client IP.

leftBehind: 2 real bookings at 2026-10-21 13:00 party 8 (X73369CM, H4CCEMX9; guests +1555555021/+1555555022) - VAL-ONLINE-004/010 evidence; each holds one table (M6, G10-T1) 17:00-19:00Z.
2 booked operator reservations at 2026-10-21 19:00/20:15 party 2 for +1555555020 (V4RM46, 8GR23Y) and 1 cancelled (CVCC65, 21:30) - VAL-ONLINE-017 test data.
1 large-party request at 2026-10-21 13:00 party 9 (BQ6DQNY6, pending_approval, guest +1555555020) - VAL-ONLINE-017/040 evidence; holds table G10-T11 17:00-19:00Z.

No live holds left behind (all 5 released, 2 converted; org-wide active holds = 0). No settings, flags or code changed. Scratch tokens under /tmp/g2-work are chmod 600 and the operator tokens have expired.
summary: 10 assertions: 6 pass (VAL-ONLINE-004, 009, 010, 012, 017, 019), 4 blocked (013, 014, 016, 040) by a shared durable rate-limit bucket. The root cause is that every direct local curl client hashes to the same 'unknown' IP, so the book_ip bucket (20/day) was exhausted by the parallel validators at ~11:26Z and POST /reservations refused every attempt for the rest of the UTC day; VAL-ONLINE-013 is additionally partially evidenced by the two real conversions from the VAL-ONLINE-004 flow, and VAL-ONLINE-017 passed with a documented route substitution (the same enforcePhoneLimits() helper exercised through /reservations/requests, 429 phone_active_limit with three active and a 201 after cancelling one).
